name: BlahDNS Browser Extension 0.2.0 preview
body:
BlahDNS Browser Extension 0.2.0 adds System, Light, and Dark appearances, the owner's BlahDNS Lite ABP default, and unsigned Firefox XPI packaging.

- Appearance is saved for settings and popup. System follows the OS. Website fingerprint values are unchanged.
- The offline default ABP snapshot comes from https://oooo.b-cdn.net/blahdns/lite_adblocker.txt and retains all 114,578 supported rules. Content-farm filtering stays separate. Combined defaults compile 126,170 domains into 921 DNR rules.
- Update list downloads a fresh default source only on request, bounded to 4 MB. Successful updates are cached locally; download, validation or storage failure preserves previous rules and cache. No startup or scheduled fetch is added.
- Downloads: Chromium ZIP, Firefox ZIP, unsigned Firefox XPI, and SHA256SUMS. The XPI and Firefox ZIP are byte-identical. Each package is about 1.03 MB.

Verification: 40 unit tests and 204 expectations; Chrome 17 integration checks, Brave 17, Firefox 18. The actual unmodified XPI installs in Firefox without optional proxy permission. Light/Dark save-button text contrast measures 5.35:1 / 10.68:1. Repeated builds produce identical ZIP/XPI hashes. Detailed source, browser, benchmark and failure/recovery records are under docs/evals/0.2.0/.

Install Chrome/Brave through chrome://extensions → Developer mode → Load unpacked with the extracted Chromium ZIP folder. Install Firefox temporarily through about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox → Load Temporary Add-on → select the intact XPI or manifest.json from the extracted Firefox ZIP. Temporary Firefox installs end at restart. Ordinary permanent Firefox installation requires Mozilla signing; this GitHub XPI is unsigned. No CRX signing or browser-store listing is included.

DoH configuration remains manual. UA/language affect request headers only; WebRTC and Firefox native fingerprint resistance are browser-wide. No telemetry, cloud settings sync, remote code, fingerprint-noise injection, CAPTCHA bypass or browser-protocol guarantee is added. Runtime dependencies remain empty. v0.1.0 is preserved.
